## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Two things should be fixed: `slugify` drops non-ASCII letters, which the pull-request description doesn't allow for, and the description has no `## Testing` section, which project policy requires.

## Changes
This pull request adds `app/slug.py` with a `slugify(title)` helper. It lowercases the title, collapses runs of characters outside `[a-z0-9]` into one hyphen, and trims hyphens from both ends. It also adds `tests/test_slug.py`, a parametrized test with four cases.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — Keep non-ASCII letters in slugs — A title like `"Café Menu"` gives `"caf-menu"`, and `"日本語"` gives `""`, because `[^a-z0-9]+` treats letters such as `é` as separators. The description says only "non-alphanumeric characters" are replaced, and `é` is alphanumeric. — Pages with accented or non-Latin titles get broken slugs or empty ones, so different pages can end up with the same URL. — Fix: Either transliterate first (for example, `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)` and drop combining marks) or match `[\W_]+` with `re.UNICODE`, then add a non-ASCII case to the parametrize list in `tests/test_slug.py`.
- PR body — correctness — Add the required `## Testing` section — The description is one paragraph with no `## Testing` section, which breaks the rule "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." (AGENTS.md:4). — Maintainers can't tell from the description how, or whether, the change was verified.
